title: The sphere's count needs resolution size 2^Theta(sqrt n)
claim: The sphere's count needs resolution size 2^Theta(sqrt n). There is an absolute constant c > 0 such that every resolution refutation of the not-all-equal formula of the octahedral knot sphere K_k (n = 4k^2 points) has size at least 2^(c k); size n^O(1) 2^O(sqrt n) suffices. Proof: a random hard-core island packing (radius 1, separation 17, uniform labels) fixes every point away from the corners with probability at least 7/(eM), M = 1141, with independence beyond distance 40; so every clause with W literals survives with probability at most (1 - q)^((W - N_c)/V); a refutation of size below 2^(alpha (c(1) k - 1 - N_c)) would leave a refutation of width below c(1) k - 1 of a restricted formula, contradicting SPHERE-SIZE-20261107-001A. Corollary (sketch): grid Sperner and Itsykson et al.'s Sperner CSP need size 2^Omega(m) in general resolution.
failure_conditions: A sampled packing with two islands closer than the separation, or coverage frequencies below the formula bound.
A gap in the random-restriction argument (coverage, locality, union bound) or in the island lemma it uses.
For the corollary: a boundary island configuration that forms a negative cycle from fixed points alone.
foundation_claim_scope: The octahedral knot spheres K_k for every k (by the proof); packing properties checked on K_16 and K_20; grid Sperner by sketch.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: the theorem by hand from the island lemma and a standard random-restriction argument; packing properties checked by Monte Carlo against the exact formula; no human or external review
validation.novelty: new as far as found: resolution size bounds for these formulas, and (by the sketched corollary) for grid Sperner in general resolution, where only tree-like size was known; the method is Dantchev-Riis local randomization.
